text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own EXCAVA'S OWN interface — visibility, liveliness, clarity, enjoyment, speed of OUR scre

name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. It flags any text or UI element below WCAG AA contrast in real time, so we catch issues before they reach users. The trade-off is slower iteration—we’ll pause to fix contrast instead of moving faster—but it prevents costly rework and ensures accessibility compliance from day one.

name: Pane
text: The live contrast checker trains designers to ignore warnings like seatbelt alarms—users will learn to dismiss them too. Instead, pre-submit gates fail because they only move the problem; a better alternative is a pre-commit hook that blocks low-contrast merges entirely, forcing immediate fixes. Settle it by testing both: measure how often designers override the live checker versus how often they bypass the gate, and track if either reduces final rework.

name: Facet
text:
Ship a pre-commit hook that blocks merges with WCAG AA contrast failures. It forces immediate fixes at the point of creation, not after the fact, so low-contrast issues never reach users. The trade-off is designer friction—some builds will pause—but it cuts rework and ensures every merge meets the standard. This beats live checkers because it stops the problem at the source, not just flags it.

name: Pane
text: The pre-commit hook doesn’t solve the seatbelt-alarm problem—it just moves the friction earlier, making designers resent the gate instead of the tool. A better alternative is a *gradual* enforcement: warn in the live checker first, then escalate to a soft pre-commit block, then hard block only after repeated violations. Settle it with a 2-week trial—if designers bypass the warnings, we’ll know the problem isn’t the timing, it’s the tool’s credibility.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Ship a *gradual* contrast enforcement system—live warnings first, soft pre-commit blocks after 3 warnings, hard pre-commit blocks only after 7 warnings—so designers learn to fix issues without resentment.

Result: A WCAG AA-compliant interface where low-contrast issues are caught early, iteratively, and without friction. Owned by Facet (visualization-w1).
